title: Tidal Bans AI Music, While Apple Music Sticks to Labels
excerpt: Streaming music service Tidal today said it plans to start blocking AI music on December 9. Any track generated entirely with AI will be removed from...
content_html:
Tuesday November 24, 2026 3:44 pm PST by Juli Clover

Streaming music service Tidal today said it plans to start blocking AI music on December 9. Any track generated entirely with AI will be removed from the platform, with Tidal rejecting AI songs in the future.


Tidal lead Robert Andersen said 43 percent of tracks uploaded in the last 90 days have been flagged as AI-generated. Approximately 29 million songs will be deleted and Tidal expects 80,000 to 85,000 songs to be rejected per day.

AI music will start disappearing on December 9 and will be "completely gone" at the beginning of 2027. AI-assisted music will continue to be allowed, since the policy is only for songs made entirely with AI tools. Tidal previously demonetized AI music, but removing it goes a step further.

Andersen said Tidal believes the move will "resonate with both artists and listeners alike" because 96 percent of AI songs get zero plays.

Apple hasn't banned AI songs from Apple Music, but it introduced AI Transparency Tags earlier this year. Apple is relying on labels and distributors to disclose when AI has been used, and it said in August that tracks "materially generated using AI" must have a "Made With AI" label.

In April, ‌Apple Music‌ VP Oliver Schusser said that more than a third of monthly uploads to ‌Apple Music‌ are 100 percent AI-generated, but AI music accounted for less than 0.5 percent of actual listening.
